name: Read a garment pattern
blurb: Commercial patterns are written in their own language — ease, grainlines, notches, darts. Learning to read one properly is what unlocks making clothes that actually fit.
gear: A simple pattern for a woven garment
Fabric for a toile, such as cheap calico
steps: Measure yourself properly and choose the size from the pattern’s body measurements, not from shop sizing.
Learn to read the finished-garment measurements and the ease built in — this tells you how it will actually sit.
Learn the markings: grainline, notches, darts, fold lines, seam allowance.
Cut on grain. Ignoring the grainline is what makes homemade clothes hang oddly.
Make a toile in cheap fabric first and fit it, adjusting the pattern rather than the good fabric.
Learn one or two standard adjustments, such as a full bust adjustment or shortening the bodice.
tips: Pattern sizes are not shop sizes and usually run several sizes larger. Ignore the number.
Nobody is standard. The toile is where fit actually happens.
proof: A garment you drafted adjustments for and made, that fits you properly.
